short_answer: Mike Lundin is an active handicapper on StatSalt, a pick site whose refund policy says all purchases are made from Wager Talk Media, LP, the company behind WagerTalk. His profile has been online since at least November 2025. On 17 Nov 2026 it sold $5 single plays, three day sport passes and all sports passes, and it showed plays graded as recently as 16 Nov 2026. In that narrow sense he is a real, current seller.

Whether his picks make money over time is a separate question. His last 20 graded plays, 12 to 16 Nov 2026, came to 13 wins and 7 losses by our count, and the sales copy claims "Profits 5 of the last 6 NBA seasons!" without naming the seasons. An outside tracker that follows his free picks showed 11 wins and 11 losses and a small loss over the last 30 days. Neither is a full record.
We found no buyer talk about him anywhere. Treat him as an unproven seller, start with the cheapest option if you try him at all, and record every pick yourself with the line and time you got it.

guarantee: We saw no guarantee on his passes. The StatSalt refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold "as is"" and "Once a product or service has been purchased, delivered, and/or viewed, no refunds will be issued." It also lists cases where no refund is given, such as games your state does not let you bet and "Undelivered email or SMS notifications". The charge appears on a card statement as "WT/SM* PICKS AND PAR".

The StatSalt FAQ answers "Are your picks guaranteed to win?" with "No picks or predictions are guaranteed." The terms say "The information contained at this site is for entertainment and amusement purposes only" and that the buyer's "exclusive remedy, shall be a refund of the price paid" or a replacement.

The page data lists a "guaranteed" option on single plays at $8, but the profile does not explain it. On WagerTalk, which shares the same parent company, the guarantee "backs your purchase with 100% in credits": if the daily package does not show an overall profit, the price comes back as account credit for a future purchase, not cash. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: The college basketball season was about two weeks old on 17 Nov 2026, so a 20 and 8 record means many plays in a short time, and it is ranked only against other StatSalt sellers. A run that short tells you little about the next month.

The last 20 list is the most useful thing on the page because it shows losses, odds and ratings. By our count it was 13 and 7, mostly at odds between minus 102 and minus 118. That is five days of plays graded by the seller.
The NBA claim names no seasons, units or prices, and we could find no trace of him selling picks anywhere before late 2025. The poker career is not backed by any name, event or result we could check.
record: Watchdog graded sample, new 22 Nov 2026. Mike Lundin does not publish a complete, time stamped log we can audit, so we built a sample from public posts that carry their plays. Watchdog captures X accounts and forum threads that post or repost picks; the ones naming Mike Lundin most often were TheGodOfCappers, EZMSports, parlaybaby002, CashoutClubX. From 22 Sep 2026 to 31 Oct 2026 we took every play our parser could read inside a Mike Lundin block, kept only those posted before the game started, removed repeats, and graded each one against the final score at one unit risked, at the odds shown or -110 when none were shown.
Result: 6 plays, 4 won, 2 lost, +1.64 units, a return of +27.3% per unit risked. By month: September 0 won, 1 lost, -1.00 units; October 4 won, 1 lost, +2.64 units.
What it means: 6 decided plays is far too few to judge.
What a buyer can verify independently: no full, time stamped log of every paid Mike Lundin pick kept by anyone other than the seller, and no court or regulator record about him.

What the seller publishes: a last 20 list on the StatSalt profile. On 17 Nov 2026 it covered 12 to 16 Nov 2026 and went 13 wins and 7 losses by our count, every play rated 3 or 4. He did not appear in the top lists of the StatSalt last 365 days leaderboard when we checked it.

A third party: GameAdvisers, a site that says it may earn sportsbook commissions, tracks his free picks. On 17 Nov 2026 it showed 11 wins and 11 losses, minus $124 and a minus 5.0% return over the last 30 days, with totals at 1 and 4. Its page labels him as part of a different network, SportsCapping Group, so its labels may not be reliable, and it covers free picks only.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Mike Lundin is nil.

customers.text: We found no buyer who posted a review, a complaint or a tracked result of Mike Lundin's paid picks. Web searches for his name returned only his own StatSalt pages and unrelated people with the same name. Our saved Reddit archive had no posts or comments naming him, the live Reddit archive search of r/sportsbook returned nothing and other subreddits timed out. StatSalt shows no reader comments or star rating on his profile. The only outside numbers are an automated tracker of his free picks, which showed him even over 30 days. There is no buyer pattern to report in either direction.

His StatSalt profile shows a 13 and 7 run over his last 20 plays and season run claims in college basketball and the NBA. These are published by the site that sells his picks, so they are marketing, not independent evidence.

TheRX daily service play thread tells members not to post picks from a list of services that includes "All Wagertalk Cappers." Neither StatSalt nor Mike Lundin is named, and the rule gives no reason, so it says nothing about his quality.

We found no thread about Mike Lundin on Reddit, TheRX, Covers or Sportsbook Review, no review on an independent site and no Better Business Bureau page. The Reddit archive search of r/sportsbook returned no posts; searches of r/sportsbetting timed out and could not be completed.

conflicts: Every record on the StatSalt profile is graded and published by StatSalt, which sells the picks. The "#1 ranked" claim compares him only with other StatSalt handicappers.
StatSalt and WagerTalk share a parent, Wager Talk Media, LP, and the same Las Vegas seller address, prices and specials. WagerTalk itself has no Mike Lundin profile.
StatSalt says it may receive a commission when a visitor opens a sportsbook or casino account through its links.
The only outside tracker, GameAdvisers, also says it may earn sportsbook commissions.
strengths: Prices are published for every option, and single plays were cheap at $5 on the day we checked.
The profile shows recent losing plays as well as wins, with the odds, the rating and the sportsbook for each.
Each play comes with a written explanation of the angle behind it.
The bio explains his rating scale from 2% to 5%, and his recent plays match it.
His free picks are tracked by an outside site, so a buyer can see how they did before paying.
concerns: No full public record. Every number on the sales page comes from the site that sells him.
His tracked free picks were 11 and 11 with a small loss over 30 days, well below the paid list's 13 and 7.
No independent buyer reviews or complaints at all, so there is nothing to weigh either way.
All sales are final, and the guarantee option on single plays is not explained on the profile.
Sales copy uses words like "CAN'T MISS" and short season runs that prove little, and the poker background cannot be checked.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A run in a listing title is not a record.
Count units, not wins. His plays are rated 3 or 4 units, so a few big losses can erase many small wins.
Read the refund policy before paying. On StatSalt all sales are final.
If you buy the guaranteed option, expect site credit, not cash, if the play loses.
Start with a single play or a one day pass before any monthly pass, and compare with his free picks.
faq: He is a real, active handicapper whose picks are sold on StatSalt at published prices, and his profile has existed since at least November 2025. We could not verify that his picks win over time, because the only full lists come from the site that sells them, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
What does the Watchdog sample of Mike Lundin show?
We graded 6 of their plays that were posted publicly before the game started, 22 Sep 2026 to 31 Oct 2026: 4 won, 2 lost, +1.64 units at one unit each. That is too few plays to judge.
How much does Mike Lundin cost?

On 17 Nov 2026 his StatSalt profile sold single plays for $5.00 and all sports passes for $39 a day, $69 for 3 days, $99 for 7 days and $299 for 30 days, plus $49.00 weekend and three day sport passes.
Does Mike Lundin have a verified record?

No. His last 20 plays were 13 and 7 by our count, graded by StatSalt. An outside tracker of his free picks showed 11 and 11 over 30 days. Nobody publishes an independent, time stamped log of every paid pick.
Can I get a refund on StatSalt?
No. The refund policy says all sales are final and no refunds are issued once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed. A guaranteed play, where offered, returns site credit rather than cash.

The StatSalt refund policy says all purchases are made from Wager Talk Media, LP, "the parent company of StatSalt." The terms give the seller address as 11035 Lavender Hill Dr, Las Vegas, NV. That is the company behind WagerTalk, which says it was founded in July 2015.
Single plays are cheap enough to test him, and each comes with a write up. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and all sales are final.
